claim: The outer membrane (OM) of Gram-negative bacteria serves as a selective permeability barrier that allows entry of essential nutrients while excluding toxic compounds, including antibiotics.
source: The outer membrane (OM) of Gram-negative bacteria serves as a selective permeability barrier that allows entry of essential nutrients while excluding toxic compounds, including antibiotics.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about the function of the outer membrane in Gram-negative bacteria.

claim: The OM is asymmetric and contains an outer leaflet of lipopolysaccharides (LPS) or lipooligosaccharides (LOS) and an inner leaflet of glycerophospholipids (GPL).
source: The OM is asymmetric and contains an outer leaflet of lipopolysaccharides (LPS) or lipooligosaccharides (LOS) and an inner leaflet of glycerophospholipids (GPL).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the composition of the outer membrane, supported by citation in the introduction section (Pelletier et al., 2013).

claim: A screen of Acinetobacter baumannii transposon mutants identified mutants with OM defects, including an ABC transporter system homologous to the Mla system in E. coli.
source: We screened Acinetobacter baumannii transposon mutants and identified a number of mutants with OM defects, including an ABC transporter system homologous to the Mla system in E. coli.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results from the transposon screen performed in this study.

claim: The Mla system in A. baumannii uses ATP hydrolysis at the inner membrane to promote GPL export to the OM.
source: We further show that this opportunistic, antibiotic-resistant pathogen uses this multicomponent protein complex and ATP hydrolysis at the inner membrane to promote GPL export to the OM.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data including stable isotope labeling experiments and dominant-negative mutant studies.

claim: The Mla system is broadly conserved in Gram-negative bacteria.
source: The broad conservation of the Mla system in Gram-negative bacteria suggests the system may play a conserved role in OM biogenesis.
evidence: This is stated as a known fact based on bioinformatic analysis and existing literature.

claim: The Mla system may play a conserved role in OM biogenesis.
source: The broad conservation of the Mla system in Gram-negative bacteria suggests the system may play a conserved role in OM biogenesis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the broad conservation of the system and the experimental findings in A. baumannii.

claim: The Mla system is important to Acinetobacter baumannii OM integrity and antibiotic sensitivity.
source: The importance of the Mla system to Acinetobacter baumannii OM integrity and antibiotic sensitivity suggests that its components may serve as new antimicrobial therapeutic targets.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing increased antibiotic sensitivity and OM permeability defects in mla mutants.

claim: Components of the Mla system may serve as new antimicrobial therapeutic targets.
source: The importance of the Mla system to Acinetobacter baumannii OM integrity and antibiotic sensitivity suggests that its components may serve as new antimicrobial therapeutic targets.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the importance of the Mla system to OM integrity and antibiotic resistance.

claim: The inner membrane (IM) is a symmetric bilayer of glycerophospholipids (GPL).
source: The inner membrane (IM) is a symmetric bilayer of glycerophospholipids (GPL), of which zwitterionic phosphatidylethanalomine (PE), acidic phosphatidylglycerol (PG), and cardiolipin (CL) are among the most widely distributed in bacteria (Zhang and Rock, 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge about bacterial membrane composition, supported by citation.

claim: Zwitterionic phosphatidylethanolamine (PE), acidic phosphatidylglycerol (PG), and cardiolipin (CL) are among the most widely distributed glycerophospholipids in bacteria.
source: The inner membrane (IM) is a symmetric bilayer of glycerophospholipids (GPL), of which zwitterionic phosphatidylethanalomine (PE), acidic phosphatidylglycerol (PG), and cardiolipin (CL) are among the most widely distributed in bacteria (Zhang and Rock, 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The asymmetric nature of the OM lipid bilayer and the structure of LPS/LOS molecules facilitates barrier function.
source: The asymmetric nature of its lipid bilayer and the structure of LPS/LOS molecules facilitates barrier function, as the core region of LPS impedes the entry of hydrophobic molecules into the cell while the acyl chains within the bilayer also help to prevent the entry of many hydrophilic compounds (Bishop, 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge about OM barrier function, supported by citation.

claim: The core region of LPS impedes the entry of hydrophobic molecules into the cell.
source: The asymmetric nature of its lipid bilayer and the structure of LPS/LOS molecules facilitates barrier function, as the core region of LPS impedes the entry of hydrophobic molecules into the cell while the acyl chains within the bilayer also help to prevent the entry of many hydrophilic compounds (Bishop, 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge about LPS function, supported by citation.

claim: The acyl chains within the bilayer help to prevent the entry of many hydrophilic compounds.
source: The asymmetric nature of its lipid bilayer and the structure of LPS/LOS molecules facilitates barrier function, as the core region of LPS impedes the entry of hydrophobic molecules into the cell while the acyl chains within the bilayer also help to prevent the entry of many hydrophilic compounds (Bishop, 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge about membrane barrier function, supported by citation.

claim: Little is known about the molecular mechanisms for transport of the GPLs necessary for OM formation and barrier function.
source: Although progress has been made in understanding many aspects of OM assembly – including the discovery of an LPS transport system and the machinery for proper folding and insertion of outer membrane proteins (Okuda and Tokuda, 2011; Okuda et al., 2016) – little is known about the molecular mechanisms for transport of the GPLs necessary for OM formation and barrier function.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field at the time of publication.

claim: Acinetobacter baumannii is an important cause of antibiotic-resistant opportunistic infections.
source: Acinetobacter baumannii is an important cause of antibiotic-resistant opportunistic infections and has significant innate resistance to disinfectants and antibiotics.
evidence: This is established knowledge about A. baumannii as a pathogen.

claim: Acinetobacter baumannii has significant innate resistance to disinfectants and antibiotics.
source: Acinetobacter baumannii is an important cause of antibiotic-resistant opportunistic infections and has significant innate resistance to disinfectants and antibiotics.
evidence: This is established knowledge about A. baumannii characteristics.

claim: Individuals with breached skin or damaged respiratory tract mucosa are most vulnerable to A. baumannii infections.
source: Similar to other Gram-negative opportunistic pathogens such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Klebsiella spp., individuals with breached skin or damaged respiratory tract mucosa are most vulnerable (Chmelnitsky et al., 2013; Abbo et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge about A. baumannii pathogenesis, supported by citations.

claim: A genetic screen identified an ABC transporter complex that promotes GPL export to the OM in A. baumannii.
source: We performed a genetic screen to identify genes important for the OM barrier of A. baumannii. This led to the identification of an ABC (ATP-binding cassette) transporter complex that promotes GPL export to the OM.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: Transporter disruption attenuates bacterial OM barrier function, resulting in increased susceptibility of A. baumannii to a wide variety of antibiotics.
source: Transporter disruption attenuates bacterial OM barrier function, resulting in increased susceptibility of A. baumannii to a wide variety of antibiotics.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data including MIC measurements and permeability assays.

claim: The homologous system in E. coli has been termed Mla for its suggested role in the maintenance of outer membrane lipid asymmetry via the removal of GPL from the outer leaflet of the OM to the IM.
source: The homologous system for E. coli has previously been termed Mla for its suggested role in the maintenance of outer membrane lipid asymmetry via the removal of GPL from the outer leaflet of the OM to the IM.
evidence: This is a statement about previous work and nomenclature in the field.

claim: There is not direct biochemical evidence that the Mla system functions to return GPL from the OM to the IM.
source: While this is a reasonable hypothesis, there is not direct biochemical evidence that the Mla system functions to return GPL from the OM to the IM.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of evidence in the field.

claim: The A. baumannii Mla system functions to promote GPL movement from the IM to the OM.
source: In this work, we present evidence that the A. baumannii Mla system functions to promote GPL movement from the IM to the OM.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: Newly synthesized GPLs accumulate at the IM of mla mutants.
source: This conclusion is based on the observation that newly synthesized GPLs accumulate at the IM of mla mutants, akin to how LPS molecules accumulate at the inner membrane in bacteria with mutations in the lpt genes encoding the LPS ABC transport system (Okuda et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by stable isotope labeling experiments.

claim: LPS molecules accumulate at the inner membrane in bacteria with mutations in the lpt genes encoding the LPS ABC transport system.
source: This conclusion is based on the observation that newly synthesized GPLs accumulate at the IM of mla mutants, akin to how LPS molecules accumulate at the inner membrane in bacteria with mutations in the lpt genes encoding the LPS ABC transport system (Okuda et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous work, supported by citation.

claim: The anterograde trafficking function of Mla might be exploited by a variety of species given the broad conservation of Mla in prokaryotic diderm organisms.
source: Given the broad conservation of Mla in prokaryotic diderm organisms, the anterograde trafficking function of Mla might be exploited by a variety of species.
evidence: This is an inference based on the conservation of the system and the findings in A. baumannii.

claim: A. baumannii carries an endogenous periplasmic phosphatase enzyme.
source: Although A. baumannii carries an endogenous periplasmic phosphatase enzyme, colonies remain white on agar plates containing XP.
evidence: This is an observation about A. baumannii biochemistry.

claim: A. baumannii colonies remain white on agar plates containing XP.
source: Although A. baumannii carries an endogenous periplasmic phosphatase enzyme, colonies remain white on agar plates containing XP.
evidence: This is an experimental observation.

claim: Lesions in genes necessary for the OM barrier function result in a blue colony phenotype on XP-containing agar plates.
source: We reasoned that lesions in genes necessary for the OM barrier function should result in a blue colony phenotype, as the XP substrate becomes accessible to the periplasmic enzyme (Strauch and Beckwith, 1988; Lopes et al., 1972).
evidence: This is the rationale for the screen, based on established knowledge and citations.

claim: Screening roughly 80,000 transposon-containing colonies for the blue colony phenotype yielded 364 blue colonies whose insertions were mapped to 58 unique genes.
source: Screening roughly 80,000 transposon-containing colonies for the blue colony phenotype yielded 364 blue colonies whose insertions were mapped to 58 unique genes (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental results.

claim: Greater than 85% of the strains identified in the screen demonstrated decreased OM barrier function compared to wild type.
source: Greater than 85% of the strains identified in the screen demonstrated decreased OM barrier function compared to wild type.
evidence: This is a quantitative summary of experimental results from permeability assays.

claim: 23 out of 58 strains with transposon insertions demonstrated OM permeability defects by NPN and EtBr uptake assays.
source: Out of the 58 strains with transposon insertions, 23 demonstrated OM permeability defects by NPN and EtBr uptake assays, and 49 out of 58 resulted in increased sensitivity to two or more antibiotics compared to the parent strain, indicating that the screen identified lesions causing OM barrier defects leading to increased permeability to small charged and hydrophobic molecules, including commonly used antibiotics.
evidence: This is a quantitative summary of experimental results.

claim: 49 out of 58 strains with transposon insertions resulted in increased sensitivity to two or more antibiotics compared to the parent strain.
source: Out of the 58 strains with transposon insertions, 23 demonstrated OM permeability defects by NPN and EtBr uptake assays, and 49 out of 58 resulted in increased sensitivity to two or more antibiotics compared to the parent strain, indicating that the screen identified lesions causing OM barrier defects leading to increased permeability to small charged and hydrophobic molecules, including commonly used antibiotics.
evidence: This is a quantitative summary of experimental results.

claim: The screen identified lesions causing OM barrier defects leading to increased permeability to small charged and hydrophobic molecules, including commonly used antibiotics.
source: Out of the 58 strains with transposon insertions, 23 demonstrated OM permeability defects by NPN and EtBr uptake assays, and 49 out of 58 resulted in increased sensitivity to two or more antibiotics compared to the parent strain, indicating that the screen identified lesions causing OM barrier defects leading to increased permeability to small charged and hydrophobic molecules, including commonly used antibiotics.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Four mutants with a blue colony phenotype contained unique transposon insertions in the genetic loci A1S_3103 and A1S_3102, predicted to encode core components (mlaF and mlaE) of a multicomponent ABC transport system.
source: Four mutants with a blue colony phenotype contained unique transposon insertions in the genetic loci A1S_3103 and A1S_3102, predicted to encode core components (mlaF and mlaE) of a multicomponent ABC transport system.
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental results from the screen.

claim: The mlaFEDCB genes are within a five-gene operon that encodes for a conserved proteobacterial ABC transport system homologous to the E. coli mla system.
source: These genes are within a five-gene operon that encodes for a conserved proteobacterial ABC transport system homologous to the E. coli mla system previously implicated in OM integrity (Malinverni and Silhavy, 2009).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic analysis and comparison to known systems, supported by citation.

claim: The E. coli mla system has been previously implicated in OM integrity.
source: These genes are within a five-gene operon that encodes for a conserved proteobacterial ABC transport system homologous to the E. coli mla system previously implicated in OM integrity (Malinverni and Silhavy, 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous work, supported by citation.

claim: MlaF and MlaE are respectively predicted to encode the nucleotide-binding and transmembrane domains of an ABC transporter.
source: The A. baumannii operon includes: mlaF and mlaE, respectively predicted to encode the nucleotide-binding and transmembrane domains of an ABC transporter; mlaD, encoding a protein containing an IM-spanning domain and a predicted periplasmic soluble domain; mlaC, encoding a soluble periplasmic protein; and mlaB, an additional gene predicted to encode a cytoplasmic sulfate transporter and anti-sigma factor antiagonist (STAS)-domain protein (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic prediction and sequence analysis.

claim: MlaD encodes a protein containing an IM-spanning domain and a predicted periplasmic soluble domain.
source: The A. baumannii operon includes: mlaF and mlaE, respectively predicted to encode the nucleotide-binding and transmembrane domains of an ABC transporter; mlaD, encoding a protein containing an IM-spanning domain and a predicted periplasmic soluble domain; mlaC, encoding a soluble periplasmic protein; and mlaB, an additional gene predicted to encode a cytoplasmic sulfate transporter and anti-sigma factor antiagonist (STAS)-domain protein (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic prediction and sequence analysis.

claim: MlaC encodes a soluble periplasmic protein.
source: The A. baumannii operon includes: mlaF and mlaE, respectively predicted to encode the nucleotide-binding and transmembrane domains of an ABC transporter; mlaD, encoding a protein containing an IM-spanning domain and a predicted periplasmic soluble domain; mlaC, encoding a soluble periplasmic protein; and mlaB, an additional gene predicted to encode a cytoplasmic sulfate transporter and anti-sigma factor antiagonist (STAS)-domain protein (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic prediction and sequence analysis.

claim: MlaB is predicted to encode a cytoplasmic sulfate transporter and anti-sigma factor antagonist (STAS)-domain protein.
source: The A. baumannii operon includes: mlaF and mlaE, respectively predicted to encode the nucleotide-binding and transmembrane domains of an ABC transporter; mlaD, encoding a protein containing an IM-spanning domain and a predicted periplasmic soluble domain; mlaC, encoding a soluble periplasmic protein; and mlaB, an additional gene predicted to encode a cytoplasmic sulfate transporter and anti-sigma factor antiagonist (STAS)-domain protein (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic prediction and sequence analysis.

claim: MlaA is a putative OM lipoprotein encoded at a different chromosomal location in A. baumannii.
source: An additional putative OM lipoprotein is encoded on mlaA, or vacJ, which is clustered with the rest of the mla operon in some Gram-negative bacteria, although it is at a different chromosomal location in A. baumannii.
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic analysis and genomic organization.

claim: MlaA has been functionally associated with the rest of the Mla components in E. coli.
source: MlaA has been functionally associated with the rest of the Mla components in E. coli, as mutations in mlaA yield comparable phenotypes to mutations in other components of the system (Strauch and Beckwith, 1988).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous work, supported by citation.

claim: Mutations in mlaA yield comparable phenotypes to mutations in other components of the Mla system in E. coli.
source: MlaA has been functionally associated with the rest of the Mla components in E. coli, as mutations in mlaA yield comparable phenotypes to mutations in other components of the system (Strauch and Beckwith, 1988).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous work, supported by citation.

claim: Chromosomal deletions of mlaC and mlaF resulted in OM permeability defects as measured by EtBr uptake assays.
source: Chromosomal deletions were created by allelic exchange, and these mutations resulted in OM permeability defects as measured by EtBr uptake assays.
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental results shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The OM defect for the ∆mlaC and ∆mlaF deletion mutants was complemented by repairing the original deletion event in the chromosome.
source: We complemented the OM defect for the ∆mlaC and ∆mlaF deletion mutants by repairing the original deletion event in the chromosome and confirmed complementation of the observed permeability defect (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental results shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Deletions in mlaF and mlaC rendered A. baumannii increasingly sensitive to a variety of antibiotics.
source: Deletions in mlaF and mlaC also rendered A. baumannii increasingly sensitive to a variety of antibiotics as determined by MIC measurements (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental results shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Increased sensitivity to antibiotics whose uptake is not mediated by OM porins is consistent with a direct effect on the membrane component of the OM permeability barrier.
source: Increased sensitivity to antibiotics whose uptake is not mediated by OM porins is consistent with a direct effect on the membrane component of the OM permeability barrier (Nikaido, 2003; Vaara, 1992).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results based on established knowledge, supported by citations.

claim: The mla mutants display increased production of extracellular carbohydrates as evidenced by crystal violet staining of pellicles.
source: In addition to OM defects, the mla mutants display phenotypes that may correlate with OM stress, including increased production of extracellular carbohydrates as evidenced by crystal violet staining of pellicles following growth in broth culture (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental results shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The increased production of extracellular carbohydrates in mla mutants may correlate with OM stress.
source: In addition to OM defects, the mla mutants display phenotypes that may correlate with OM stress, including increased production of extracellular carbohydrates as evidenced by crystal violet staining of pellicles following growth in broth culture (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: The Mla system plays a role in the maintenance of the outer membrane barrier of A. baumannii.
source: These data indicate a role for Mla in the maintenance of the outer membrane barrier of A. baumannii.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data presented.

claim: MlaF contains the consensus sequence GxxxxGKT at residues 49–56, characteristic of a Walker A motif.
source: The cytoplasmic ATPase component of the Mla system, MlaF, contains the consensus sequence GxxxxGKT at residues 49–56, characteristic of a Walker A motif.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis of MlaF.

claim: MlaF contains the sequence LIMYDE at residues 173–178, typical of a Walker B motif.
source: Downstream residues 173–178 contain the sequence LIMYDE, typical of a Walker B motif.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis of MlaF.

claim: The Walker motifs form highly conserved structures critical for nucleotide binding and hydrolysis.
source: The Walker motifs form highly conserved structures critical for nucleotide binding and hydrolysis (Walker et al., 1982).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Walker motifs, supported by citation.

claim: The lysine residue of the Walker A motif is essential for the hydrolysis of ATP.
source: The lysine residue of the Walker A motif is particularly essential for the hydrolysis of ATP.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Walker A motif function.

claim: Mutations in the Walker A lysine residue inhibit nucleotide binding and render the protein inactive.
source: Mutations in this lysine residue are inhibited for nucleotide binding, and the mutated protein is rendered inactive (Hanson and Whiteheart, 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Walker A motif mutations, supported by citation.

claim: ATPase mutants in the key lysine residue have a dominant-negative effect on ATP hydrolysis when co-expressed with their wild-type ATPase counterparts.
source: Additionally, ATPase mutants in the key lysine residue have been shown to have a dominant-negative effect on ATP hydrolysis when co-expressed with their wild-type ATPase counterparts, as typical ABC transporters have a structural requirement for two functional nucleotide-binding proteins which dimerize upon substrate transport (Davidson and Sharma, 1997; Wilkens, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge about ABC transporter ATPases, supported by citations.

claim: Typical ABC transporters have a structural requirement for two functional nucleotide-binding proteins which dimerize upon substrate transport.
source: Additionally, ATPase mutants in the key lysine residue have been shown to have a dominant-negative effect on ATP hydrolysis when co-expressed with their wild-type ATPase counterparts, as typical ABC transporters have a structural requirement for two functional nucleotide-binding proteins which dimerize upon substrate transport (Davidson and Sharma, 1997; Wilkens, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge about ABC transporter structure and function, supported by citations.

claim: Expression of MlaFK55L in wild type A. baumannii had a dominant-negative effect on membrane permeability as measured by EtBr uptake.
source: We observed that expression of MlaFK55L in wild type A. baumannii had a dominant-negative effect on membrane permeability as measured by EtBr uptake (Figure 1C), and expression of MlaFK55L also resulted in increased exopolysaccharide production as demonstrated by increased staining by crystal violet (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental results shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Expression of MlaFK55L resulted in increased exopolysaccharide production as demonstrated by increased staining by crystal violet.
source: We observed that expression of MlaFK55L in wild type A. baumannii had a dominant-negative effect on membrane permeability as measured by EtBr uptake (Figure 1C), and expression of MlaFK55L also resulted in increased exopolysaccharide production as demonstrated by increased staining by crystal violet (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental results shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Expression of MlaFK55L rendered A. baumannii more sensitive to a variety of antibiotics, resulting in reduced MICs.
source: Correspondingly, expression of MlaFK55L rendered A. baumannii more sensitive to a variety of antibiotics, resulting in reduced MICs when compared to A. baumannii expressing the empty pMMBkan vector (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental results shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Expression of a defective ATPase results in a dominant-negative mutant with a comparable phenotype to deletion of components of the mla operon.
source: Therefore, expression of a defective ATPase results in a dominant-negative mutant with a comparable phenotype to deletion of components of the mla operon.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data comparing MlaFK55L expression to deletion mutants.

claim: ATP hydrolysis by MlaF is required for the maintenance of OM barrier function in A. baumannii.
source: These results demonstrate a requirement for ATP hydrolysis by MlaF for the maintenance of OM barrier function in A. baumannii, and indicate that the phenotypes of deletion mutants were likely a result of a lack of transport function, rather than formation of a toxic incomplete membrane protein complex.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the dominant-negative experiments.

claim: The phenotypes of deletion mutants were likely a result of a lack of transport function, rather than formation of a toxic incomplete membrane protein complex.
source: These results demonstrate a requirement for ATP hydrolysis by MlaF for the maintenance of OM barrier function in A. baumannii, and indicate that the phenotypes of deletion mutants were likely a result of a lack of transport function, rather than formation of a toxic incomplete membrane protein complex.
evidence: This is an inference based on the dominant-negative experiments.

claim: Affinity purification of MlaB revealed three additional bands, with sizes corresponding to MlaF, MlaD, and MlaE, confirmed by MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry analysis.
source: Affinity purification of MlaB revealed three additional bands, with sizes corresponding to MlaF, MlaD, and MlaE (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) and confirmed by MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry analysis, indicating that these four proteins form a stable complex.
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental results from protein purification and mass spectrometry.

claim: MlaF, MlaD, MlaE, and MlaB form a stable complex.
source: Affinity purification of MlaB revealed three additional bands, with sizes corresponding to MlaF, MlaD, and MlaE (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) and confirmed by MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry analysis, indicating that these four proteins form a stable complex.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the co-purification and mass spectrometry data.

claim: MlaC was not detected in the purified complex, suggesting it might interact only transiently with the other components.
source: We did not detect MlaC, suggesting it might interact only transiently with the other components, consistent with results recently reported by Thong et al. (2016).
evidence: This is an inference based on the absence of MlaC in the purified complex, supported by citation to similar findings.

claim: The abMlaBDEF complex is uniformly dispersed in vitreous ice.
source: This complex is uniformly dispersed in vitreous ice (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A), and 2D classification demonstrated the presence of a range of views suitable for structure determination (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a direct observation from cryo-EM sample preparation.

claim: 2D classification of abMlaBDEF demonstrated the presence of a range of views suitable for structure determination.
source: This complex is uniformly dispersed in vitreous ice (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A), and 2D classification demonstrated the presence of a range of views suitable for structure determination (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a direct report of cryo-EM data analysis results.

claim: A structure of abMlaBDEF was obtained to a resolution of 8.7 Å from ~14,000 particles.
source: Following 2D- and 3D-classification, we obtained a final dataset of ~14,000 particles with which we obtained a structure to a resolution of 8.7 Å (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is a direct report of the cryo-EM structure determination results.

claim: MlaD localizes to the periplasmic side of the IM in the abMlaBDEF complex.
source: Based on the bioinformatically-predicted localization of individual proteins and work recently performed on the similar E. coli Mla complex (ecMlaBDEF) (Thong et al., 2016), we propose that MlaD localizes to the periplasmic side of the IM, MlaE forms the central transmembrane region, and MlaF and MlaB form the bottom layer on the cytoplasmic face of the IM with two visible hetero-dimers (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is a proposal based on bioinformatic prediction and comparison to the E. coli complex, supported by citation.

claim: MlaE forms the central transmembrane region in the abMlaBDEF complex.
source: Based on the bioinformatically-predicted localization of individual proteins and work recently performed on the similar E. coli Mla complex (ecMlaBDEF) (Thong et al., 2016), we propose that MlaD localizes to the periplasmic side of the IM, MlaE forms the central transmembrane region, and MlaF and MlaB form the bottom layer on the cytoplasmic face of the IM with two visible hetero-dimers (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is a proposal based on bioinformatic prediction and comparison to the E. coli complex, supported by citation.

claim: MlaF and MlaB form the bottom layer on the cytoplasmic face of the IM with two visible hetero-dimers in the abMlaBDEF complex.
source: Based on the bioinformatically-predicted localization of individual proteins and work recently performed on the similar E. coli Mla complex (ecMlaBDEF) (Thong et al., 2016), we propose that MlaD localizes to the periplasmic side of the IM, MlaE forms the central transmembrane region, and MlaF and MlaB form the bottom layer on the cytoplasmic face of the IM with two visible hetero-dimers (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is a proposal based on bioinformatic prediction and comparison to the E. coli complex, supported by citation.

claim: The structure of ecMlaBDEF was reported recently at lower resolution.
source: We note that the structure of ecMlaBDEF, at lower resolution, was reported recently (Ekiert et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about recent literature, supported by citation.

claim: The overall features of the abMlaBDEF and ecMlaBDEF structures are identical.
source: The overall features of both structures, solved independently, are identical, suggesting that they correspond to the correct structure for the complex.
evidence: This is a comparison of the two independently determined structures.

claim: The limited resolution of the ecMlaBDEF complex structure did not allow modeling of its individual subunits.
source: However, the limited resolution of the ecMlaBDEF complex structure did not allow modeling of its individual subunits, in contrast to the abMlaBDEF structure reported here.
evidence: This is a comparison of the capabilities of the two structures based on their resolutions.

claim: A clear six-fold symmetry is present for the region of the map attributed to MlaD.
source: We note that a clear six-fold symmetry is present for the region of the map attributed to MlaD (Figure 2B), despite the fact that we only imposed a 2-fold symmetry averaging.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the cryo-EM map.

claim: The six-fold symmetry of MlaD agrees with the proposed hexameric state of its E. coli homologue.
source: This agrees with the proposed hexameric state of its E. coli homologue (ecMlaD) (Thong et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous work on the E. coli system, supported by citation.

claim: The abMlaD hexameric model is at a low-energy minimum.
source: The obtained abMlaD hexameric model is at a low-energy minimum (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B) and fits the EM map density well (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is a result from computational modeling and energy minimization.

claim: The abMlaD hexameric model fits the EM map density well.
source: The obtained abMlaD hexameric model is at a low-energy minimum (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B) and fits the EM map density well (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is a result from fitting the model to the cryo-EM density.

claim: A crystal structure of the periplasmic domain of ecMlaD formed a crystallographic hexamer.
source: A crystal structure of the periplasmic domain of ecMlaD published recently (Ekiert et al., 2017) formed a crystallographic hexamer, suggesting that this corresponds to the native hexomeric arrangement for this domain.
evidence: This is a statement about recent literature, supported by citation.

claim: The crystallographic ecMlaD hexamer suggests that this corresponds to the native hexomeric arrangement for this domain.
source: A crystal structure of the periplasmic domain of ecMlaD published recently (Ekiert et al., 2017) formed a crystallographic hexamer, suggesting that this corresponds to the native hexomeric arrangement for this domain.
evidence: This is an inference based on the crystallographic observation, supported by citation.

claim: The abMlaD hexameric model is very similar to the crystallographic ecMlaD structure.
source: Our abMlaD hexameric model is very similar to the crystallographic ecMlaD structure (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C), supporting the proposed domain arrangement in the MlaBDEF complex.
evidence: This is a comparison of the model to the crystal structure.

claim: One region of density in the EM map is not accounted for by the MlaD hexamer model.
source: We note, however, that one region of density in the EM map is not accounted for by our MlaD hexamer model (Figure 2B).
